summary_of_change:
In contrast to the market's pessimistic projections, EDU's execution across the 4 consecutive quarters of FY2026 (ending May 31, 2026) demonstrates broad-based operational strength and margin leverage. Full-year FY2026 net revenues reached $5,661.3M (+15.5% YoY), with Q4 FY2026 revenue accelerating 23.0% YoY to $1,529.5M, establishing a real-time annualized run-rate of $6,118.0M. Non-GAAP operating income surged 34.7% YoY in Q4 to $110.0M, driving full-year GAAP net income to $475.2M (+27.8% YoY). Core gross margins stabilized at 53.7%, confirming that the brand retains substantial pricing power in non-academic and adult test prep programs.

Operational volume metrics confirm robust customer acquisition. Non-academic tutoring enrollments reached 1,072,000, while active paid smart learning device users expanded to 326,000 across 60 target cities. Cash flow dynamics remain exceptional: deferred revenue grew 14.8% YoY to $2,242.9M, highlighting the strength of EDU's negative working capital model. Management is aggressively deploying its cash pile, announcing a $500M capital return package for FY2027 ($300M cash dividend and $200M share buyback), fully supported by $5,560.3M in total cash and investments against only $110.0M in total debt ($4,840.0M net cash).

market_pricing_in:
Mr. Market is pricing New Oriental (EDU) at a highly skeptical valuation of 10.0x P/OE and a mere 4.9x EV/OE, reflecting deep-seated anxieties regarding the sustainability of its post-regulatory business model. The primary concern centers on whether the rapid growth in non-academic tutoring and AI-enabled learning devices represents a temporary, post-pandemic pent-up demand bubble rather than a durable compounding runway. Investors fear that the Chinese regulatory apparatus could once again intervene if non-academic tutoring begins to resemble the forbidden curriculum-based tutoring of the pre-2021 Double Reduction era. Furthermore, sell-side desks at Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs remain cautious over margin compression from rising customer acquisition costs, hardware price competition, and East Buy's structural live-streaming traffic fragmentation following the high-profile departure of star influencer Dong Yuhui.

This valuation disconnect creates a stark asymmetry. Mr. Market is treating EDU's current normalized owner earnings of $5.88 per share as peak, unsustainable profits on the verge of terminal decay. In doing so, the market is completely discounting the company's massive net cash position of $29.51 per share—which covers over 50% of the current stock price—and ignoring the robust, cash-generative nature of its negative working capital cycle. By pricing the enterprise at an implied EV/OE of under 5x, the market is demanding an extreme margin of safety for a business that continues to grow its top-line at double-digit rates and boasts an audited owner ROIC of 93.6%.
why_it_might_be_right:
While the market's pessimism appears extreme, bear thesis mechanics are rooted in real operational vulnerabilities. Should Chinese regulators enact secondary crackdowns on implicit curriculum tutoring, or if hardware giants trigger price wars in AI learning devices, EDU's unit economics would face immediate margin degradation. Furthermore, persistent geopolitical frictions continue to cap growth in high-margin overseas study consulting.

The forensic unit breakdown of this downside case illustrates severe reverse operating leverage:

1. Starting Baseline: The analysis begins with a starting normalized Owner Earnings of $5.88 per share ($963.8M total) and a balance sheet holding $+29.51 per share in net cash ($4,840M total).

2. Forensic Business Headwinds: The primary risk to the thesis is a combination of renewed regulatory tightening on implicit curriculum tutoring, severe margin compression in the AI learning device segment due to price wars with domestic hardware giants, and structural deceleration in overseas study consulting.

3. Skeptic Unit Attrition: Under this downside scenario, non-academic tutoring enrollments contract by 15% to 911,200, while active paid smart learning device users drop to 245,000 as parents push back against hardware subscription fees.

4. Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation: Due to sticky lease obligations across 1,534 learning centers and fixed teacher base salaries, a 15% drop in volume triggers reverse operating leverage. Revenue falls to $5,200.0M, and the owner cash margin compresses from 15.75% to 12.5%, resulting in a degraded Skeptic Year-3 Owner Earnings of $3.96 per share ($650.0M total).

5. Downside Risk Valuation Floor: Applying a conservative trough multiple of 6.0x P/OE (reflecting a narrow moat under regulatory duress) to the degraded $3.96 per share in Owner Earnings yields an operating business value of $23.76. Adding a conservative ending net cash position of $30.00 per share establishes a Downside Floor Target of $53.76 per share.

what_if_it_keeps_going_that_way:
Extrapolating current operational momentum through a disciplined bottom-up unit framework reveals significant upside potential over a 3-year horizon:

1. Starting Unit Baseline: The baseline models 1,072,000 non-academic tutoring enrollments and 326,000 active paid smart learning device users across 60 cities, monetized via tuition per course, AI hardware/subscriptions, and test prep fees, delivering an annualized revenue run-rate of $6,118.0M.

2. 3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation: Bottom-up expansion projects non-academic tutoring enrollments to grow to 1,450,000 by Year 3, while active paid smart learning device users expand to 450,000 as EDU deepens city-level penetration across its existing 1,534 center network.

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue (Units × Monetization): Multiplying projected Year 3 unit volumes by stable realized monetization rates generates Projected Year 3 Revenue of $8,200.0M, representing an achievable 10.3% bottom-up CAGR from the current run-rate.

4. Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings: Deducting cash operating expenses—$3,796.6M in COGS, $1,886.0M in S&M, $820.0M in R&D, $220.0M in maintenance CapEx, and $165.4M in real cash/dilutive SBC—from Year 3 Revenue yields Projected Year 3 Owner Earnings of $1,312.0M ($8.00/sh across 164.0M diluted shares), reflecting a cash margin of 16.0%.

5. Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge: Starting Net Cash of $4,840.0M + Cumulative 3Y FCF of $3,400.0M - Cumulative Buybacks of $600.0M - Cumulative Growth CapEx of $640.0M results in an Ending Year 3 Net Cash position of $7,000.0M, or $42.68 per share.

6. Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return: With Year 3 Owner Earnings YoY growth projected at g₃ = 11.0% (Steady Compounding), we strictly apply a 13.0x P/OE exit multiple from the Narrow Moat Matrix. Year 3 Owner Earnings of $8.00 per share multiplied by 13.0x ($104.00) plus Ending Net Cash of $42.68 per share yields an Intrinsic Fair Value Target of $146.68 per share, delivering an expected 3-year annualized return (IRR) of 35.9% per annum from today's $58.49 price.

What the Market is Pricing In

Mr. Market is pricing New Oriental (EDU) at a highly skeptical valuation of 10.0x P/OE and a mere 4.9x EV/OE, reflecting deep-seated anxieties regarding the sustainability of its post-regulatory business model. The primary concern centers on whether the rapid growth in non-academic tutoring and AI-enabled learning devices represents a temporary, post-pandemic pent-up demand bubble rather than a durable compounding runway. Investors fear that the Chinese regulatory apparatus could once again intervene if non-academic tutoring begins to resemble the forbidden curriculum-based tutoring of the pre-2021 Double Reduction era. Furthermore, sell-side desks at Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs remain cautious over margin compression from rising customer acquisition costs, hardware price competition, and East Buy's structural live-streaming traffic fragmentation following the high-profile departure of star influencer Dong Yuhui.

This valuation disconnect creates a stark asymmetry. Mr. Market is treating EDU's current normalized owner earnings of $5.88 per share as peak, unsustainable profits on the verge of terminal decay. In doing so, the market is completely discounting the company's massive net cash position of $29.51 per share—which covers over 50% of the current stock price—and ignoring the robust, cash-generative nature of its negative working capital cycle. By pricing the enterprise at an implied EV/OE of under 5x, the market is demanding an extreme margin of safety for a business that continues to grow its top-line at double-digit rates and boasts an audited owner ROIC of 93.6%.
